description: The Metal Rabbit in Chinese astrology: personality, Metal element traits, 1951 and 2011 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Metal Rabbit is the Rabbit born in a Metal year, one of five versions of the fourth animal. It combines the Rabbit's gentleness with Metal's qualities. Metal Rabbit years between 1924 and 2044 are 1951 and 2011. The Rabbit's fixed element is Wood.

sections.heading: The Metal Rabbit personality
paragraphs: The Metal Rabbit is something of a paradox: a gentle animal under a sharp, decisive stem. Metal controls Wood, and the Rabbit's fixed element is Wood, so the year element is said to press on the animal's nature and give it a clearer outline. Metal Rabbits are often depicted as more ambitious, discerning and self-assured than most Rabbits, with exacting standards in their work and their surroundings. They keep the sign's tact and good taste but add resolve, and they may surprise people with how firmly they hold a position. The pressure from Metal can also produce inner tension. Perfectionism, guardedness and a private tendency to brood over criticism are common themes in descriptions of this combination.

Metal is the element of autumn and harvest, and a Metal year is traditionally said to sharpen whatever animal it meets. Descriptions associate it with determination, discipline, clear judgement and a strong code of principle. Metal-year people are often portrayed as decisive, self-reliant and willing to do difficult things because they are right. The element is linked with refinement and with cutting away what is unnecessary, so it tends to bring focus and high standards. Its traditional shadow is rigidity: Metal can become inflexible, proud or emotionally guarded, preferring to be correct over being close, and finding it hard to bend once a position is taken.

sections.heading: Metal Rabbit at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Metal is usually linked with discipline, precision and principled leadership. Metal-year people are often described as the ones who set standards, cut through confusion and finish what they start, which suits law, engineering, finance, surgery, editing and any role that values exactness. They tend to work well alone and lead by example. The traditional caution is inflexibility: a Metal stem can dismiss ideas that arrive untidily, so practising curiosity before judgement usually makes them better leaders.

The Metal Rabbit pairs refined taste with a surprising backbone. Readings suit it to curation, jewellery, legal drafting, fine printing, private banking and design direction, where high standards and discretion are prized. It likes clear rules and the chance to polish work until it is genuinely excellent, whereas sloppy deadlines and noisy open-plan floors wear it down. With a partner, the Metal Rabbit is devoted and quietly protective, though it shows feeling through considered gestures more than words. Privacy and respect for its boundaries are non-negotiable. Discord usually comes from perfectionism turned on the relationship itself: a cool, critical silence when a loved one falls short of a standard that was never actually spoken.

sections.heading: Metal Rabbit years and dates
paragraphs: Between 1924 and 2044 the Metal Rabbit years are 1951 (February 6, 1951 to January 26, 1952) and 2011 (February 3, 2011 to January 22, 2012). Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1951 anyone born before Feb 6 is a Metal Tiger, not a Metal Rabbit. The combination returns every sixty years, since five elements cycle through twelve animals and only meet the same pairing again after five rounds of the zodiac. Every Metal Rabbit year is Yin, matching the Rabbit's own polarity.

Chinese almanacs call the combination Xin-Mao, joining the heavenly stem Xin to the earthly branch Mao. Births just before each new year fall in the Metal Tiger year (before February 6, 1951) and the Metal Tiger year (before February 3, 2011), and births in the weeks after each Metal Rabbit year ends belong to the Water Dragon. The new year itself fell on a Tuesday in 1951 and Thursday in 2011.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Metal Rabbit
paragraphs: Easing self-criticism is usually the most useful work for a Metal Rabbit. Separating 'good enough to share' from 'flawless' allows more of their fine work to reach the world. Because they can appear cool when they are actually anxious, explaining their reasoning to colleagues and partners helps others read them correctly. Art, music and time in nature tend to soften Metal's edge and return them to the Rabbit's natural calm. It also helps to choose a few areas where precision matters and let the rest be loose. When their discernment is matched with warmth, Metal Rabbits are respected for both quality and kindness.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Metal Rabbit shares the Rabbit's San He trine with the Goat and Pig (the Wood trine), its Liu He bond with the Dog, and its Liu Chong clash with the Rooster. The element adds a second layer: another Metal sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Metal in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Metal Rabbit years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1951 (from February 6, 1951) and 2011 (from February 3, 2011). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Metal Rabbit's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Metal and the Rabbit's fixed element is Wood; in the five-element cycles metal controls Wood. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Metal Rabbit?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Goat and Pig (San He) and the Dog (Liu He). The Rooster is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Metal Rabbit called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Xin-Mao. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Metal stem Xin, followed by its earthly branch, here Mao for the Rabbit, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Metal Rabbit different from other Rabbits?
faq.answer: All Rabbits share gentleness, tact and refined taste. The Metal year element changes the tone: metal is the element of autumn and harvest, and a Metal year is traditionally said to sharpen whatever animal it meets.
